source_review.notes: Checked official NASA Risk Management Handbook v2 Parts 1 and 2; current NPR 8000.4C Appendices/Chapters covering dispositions, mitigation, closure, acceptance, roles, concurrence, risk takers and objectives-driven management; current Technical Risk Management guidance; current SMA risk-management index; active GSFC-HDBK-8005 record; and Software Engineering Handbook CRM guidance. All ten final references returned HTTP 200. An obsolete IV&V PDF URL initially returned 404 and was replaced before completion with current NPR 8000.4C Chapter 1. The chapter distinguishes mitigation, contingency, acceptance, closure/elevation, evidence of effectiveness, aggregate risk and appropriate authority.

evidence: Reviewed pre/post response profiles, net-benefit aid, conjunctive retirement gate, evidence-driven state transition, expected consequence difference, trigger function, and retirement record tuple.
Confirmed scenario, response, baseline/configuration, objectives, evidence, probability, consequence vector, uncertainty, secondary risk, cost/resource effect and authority remain distinct.
Confirmed expected-value expressions are explicitly limited to calibrated probabilities and cardinal common-basis consequences.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Notation separates action implementation, effectiveness evidence, residual risk, acceptance and closure rather than collapsing them into one score.

evidence: Executed risk-response-retirement-check and reproduced baseline expected consequence 6.00, residual 0.80, mitigation cost 2.00 and net expected reduction 3.20.
Confirmed all six declared closure criteria and tested contingency yield eligibility for retirement review rather than automatic closure.
Recomputed Exercise 1 baseline 10, response A residual 2.5/net 4.5 and response B residual 1.0/net 4.0.
numerical_recomputation.notes: All displayed arithmetic agrees with independent recomputation and is repeatedly bounded as a scalar teaching aid rather than acceptance authority.

evidence: Confirmed the risk-state arrow requires implemented response plus evidence and may change scenario, configuration, likelihood, consequence and uncertainty.
Confirmed net expected reduction subtracts residual expectation and action cost from baseline expectation but requires secondary/portfolio and noncompensatory outcomes outside the scalar expression.
Confirmed the retirement expression is conjunction across scenario, implementation, effectiveness, residual, handoff and authority criteria, so completed work alone is insufficient.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Trigger implication is explicitly conditional on observable data quality, threshold/hysteresis, decision lead, owner and executable response.

evidence: Challenged vague response targets, actions unrelated to mechanisms, late mitigation, planned/unimplemented controls, nominal tests, unexplained anomalies, double credit, common-control failures, degradation and false independence.

Reviewed information versus physical mitigation, secondary/migrated risks, operator/equity burden, contractual transfer, contingency/reserve distinctions, trigger lead, false positives/negatives and untested recovery.

Reviewed implicit acceptance through release/waiver/delivery, local versus aggregate thresholds, provider/acquirer handoff, affected risk takers, closure after occurrence, weakened criteria, deleted history and stigma around reopening.
Reviewed all ten examples and five answers for causal effect, timing, implementation/effectiveness evidence, residual/aggregate state, authority, handoff, closure and reopening.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Consequential applications still require applicable safety, security, privacy, human-factors, ethics, legal, environmental, cost/schedule, supplier, operational, public-health, community and affected-risk-taker review.

evidence: Traced causal response linkage, alternative breadth, credited-control work/evidence, forecast-versus-verified effectiveness, uncertainty/control reliability, secondary/aggregate risks, distinct mitigation/contingency/reserve/acceptance, timely triggers, acceptance package, predeclared criteria, preserved closure history and reopening throughout the module.
Confirmed current/inherent/planned/residual profiles and control configurations prevent baseline double counting.
Confirmed closing because a risk occurred creates issue/successor links rather than mislabeling occurrence as mitigation.
Confirmed monitoring handoff includes resources, owner, indicators and reopening conditions before retirement.
invariant_checking.notes: Activity, implementation, effectiveness, reduction, residual acceptance and retirement remain separate governed states.

proof_review.notes: The chapter presents response and retirement relations but no theorem proof.

proof_sketch_labeling.notes: No passage is presented as a proof sketch.

evidence: Reviewed mitigated, reduced, effective, verified, validated, residual, accepted, closed, retired, tested, representative, independent, complete, safe and current language for explicit evidence scope.

Test, exercise, inspection, simulation, prototype, supplier, operator, monitoring, incident and operational evidence remains conditioned on configuration, population/environment, duration, uncertainty, anomalies, provenance and limitations.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No external review is claimed. Completed actions, green scores, expected-value improvement, passed nominal tests or independent review are never presented as proof of acceptable or zero risk.

conceptual_review.notes: Internal conceptual review checked avoidance/elimination, mitigation/reduction, transfer/share, acceptance, contingency, indicators/triggers, inherent/current/residual risk, secondary/migrated risk, mitigation plan, retirement and closure package. Information, physical control, reserve, contingency, acceptance, closure and deletion remain distinct.

practitioner_review.notes: Internal practitioner-oriented review checked task versus effectiveness, information action, late mitigation, secondary security/emergency risk, transfer, trigger lead, contingency exercise, implicit acceptance, realized-risk closure, reopening, supplier qualification, rare emergency training, shared-cloud portfolio and wildfire-smoke schools. Each ties causal work to evidence, residual governance and learning.

pedagogical_review.notes: Internal pedagogical review confirmed progression from risk revalidation/target through alternative generation, causal mapping/comparison, information distinction, controlled planning/timing/measures, implementation/effectiveness/common cause, secondary risk, indicators/triggers/contingency, residual/aggregate/acceptance, retirement/closure/audit/reopening and honest burn-down. Ten examples and five complete answers require expected-value arithmetic, plan design, evidence critique, aggregate analysis and sociotechnical governance.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic, practitioner, risk-management, systems, architecture, safety, security, privacy, human-factors, ethics, legal, environmental, cost, schedule, supplier, operations, verification, validation, public-health, education, community, accessibility, equity, or affected-risk-taker review is claimed.
